# BUMBLE-BOT DESIGN GUIDE
### Official Visual Language for the BumbleBot Learning Companion System

---

## OVERVIEW

**BumbleBot** is a tabletop AI-robotics kit aimed at kids aged 6–12 that teaches computational thinking through physical play. The robot itself is a palm-sized hexagonal device with expressive LED "eyes" and magnetic snap-on modules (wheels, arms, sensors). The companion app provides coding missions, animated feedback, and a persistent mascot that grows alongside the child's skill level.

The design language — called **Honeycomb** — draws from the geometry of beehives to communicate ideas the product genuinely embodies: *collective intelligence, structured creativity, and small pieces building something larger.* Everything hexagonal. Everything warm. Nothing intimidating.

---

## TARGET USERS

| Audience | Role | Design Need |
|---|---|---|
| **Children 6–12** | Primary users | Immediate delight, readable at a glance, forgiving error states |
| **Parents & caregivers** | Purchase decision, onboarding | Trust signals, legibility, premium but approachable feel |
| **Teachers & librarians** | Classroom deployment | Clear information hierarchy, printable materials, accessible contrast |

The Honeycomb language must work simultaneously as *a toy* (joyful, surprising) and *a tool* (consistent, learnable). These goals don't conflict — they inform each other.

---

## COLOR SYSTEM

The palette is called **The Hive.** It derives from real bumblebee coloration, then nudges each hue toward screen-safe, high-contrast values.

### Core Colors

| Name | Hex | Role |
|---|---|---|
| **Queen Yellow** | `#FFCC00` | Primary brand, CTAs, mascot body, physical robot accent ring |
| **Drone Black** | `#1A1A2E` | Primary text, deep UI backgrounds, robot chassis |
| **Honeycomb Amber** | `#E8860A` | Hover states, progress indicators, warm shadow tones |
| **Pollen White** | `#FFF9EC` | Page backgrounds, card fills — not pure white, always warm |
| **Meadow Green** | `#3DBD72` | Success states, correct answers, "mission complete" moments |
| **Scout Red** | `#E84545` | Errors and warnings only — used sparingly and always paired with iconography |

### Usage Rules

- **Queen Yellow** never appears as body text on Pollen White — contrast ratio falls short of WCAG AA. Use Drone Black for all type over yellow backgrounds.
- The palette intentionally has no blue. In a market saturated with blue-heavy tech brands, the absence is a signal.
- UI surfaces use **tints, not additional hues.** Pollen White at 60% opacity over Drone Black gives you the dark-mode card color. No new swatches; the system stays closed.

---

## TYPOGRAPHY

The type system is called **The Waggle Stack** (after the bee dance that communicates direction and distance — information encoded in motion).

### Typefaces

| Role | Face | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Display / Headlines** | **Nunito ExtraBold** | Rounded terminals read as friendly without being babyish; works large and small |
| **Body / UI** | **Nunito Regular / SemiBold** | Family consistency reduces cognitive load; SemiBold replaces italic for clarity on screens |
| **Code / Mission Blocks** | **JetBrains Mono** | Children are learning real code syntax; the coding surface uses a genuine monospace to normalize the visual register of programming |

Both faces are open-source (Google Fonts / JetBrains). Classroom and parent printables cost nothing to render correctly.
